body:
This might be a duplicate of #569.  Apparently  #2842 is a similar issue, but not reproducible.   

You can reproduce the [two failing](https://black.vercel.app/?version=main&state=_Td6WFoAAATm1rRGAgAhARYAAAB0L-Wj4AFYAMhdAD2IimZxl1N_WlwxRhR7MSgFUcTLI8hLawxlAyW2NgE9_lTiPPyVhMGc-wvzgZl0QYztn58fCHpBlL-a2htWFNgwe8bVc01IX4EjBLkGYlaYohJ-2bRTdv7gjwOr1uudK6ZmpF9E9tU27We1Mlly8yLc50aOfTTe7LIK_mrJ2gpIqAbdMQ44xmcpFpB8F2_bnp97Ld90fvCqi7QcroGeYUxwuojLrPrc-fpXPqEM2zJ-m-Z6nFtYVLmExbYJdJExQxyqGVA_CpfTAJ0kilQWFbBPAAHkAdkCAACEhjgrscRn-wIAAAAABFla) snippets in the [playground](https://black.vercel.app/?version=main&state=_Td6WFoAAATm1rRGAgAhARYAAAB0L-Wj4AEaALZdAD2IimZxl1N_WlwxRhR7MSgFUcTLI8hLawxlAyW2NgE9_lTiPPyVhMGc-wvzgZl0QYztn58fCHpBlL-a2htWFNgwe8bVc01IX4EjBLkGYlaYohJ-2bRTdv7gjwOr1uudK6ZmpF9E9tORRjfI9AUyG1_kW1BaoS-Lo4kWvjlORgc29LGpAPqz_36DBHaL1-DpGaY5BaQDSt3rxen-cEcaY_jZYZq_djk1141RzrrfR6h24JetehcAAAAAdY5BviE6MKwAAdIBmwIAAILyBsixxGf7AgAAAAAEWVo=).

I'm leaving this open so that the team can decide if its the same problem or not.

FWIW, we do require the comments to be in the same block, although [the documentation](https://black.readthedocs.io/en/stable/the_black_code_style/current_style.html?highlight=fmt%3A%20off#code-style) could be clearer about it.

As to your other concern, I managed to simplify a bit: [playground](https://black.vercel.app/?version=main&state=_Td6WFoAAATm1rRGAgAhARYAAAB0L-Wj4AC0AFxdAD2IimZxl1N_WlXnON2nzNX9HFvHx6cBGYYzxnKDXUC9bWnmZzxb2iGsQymhw57kOZ1YCFANQYZgKwu2GQTPW_J2EDHRMjoxdYk2059SL25H6MSVOWD5Q63tef_gAKllYQb7vB0hAAF4tQEAAABwu79EscRn-wIAAAAABFla).

```python
class Foo:
    # fmt: off
    1
    # fmt: one

class Bar:
    # fmt: off
    1
    # fmt: on
```

produces a "cannot parse" on Bar's line "1". Removing the Foo definition and unindenting the body works, but removing Bar similarly produces code not equivalent to the source.
Definitely related, but I propose we edit this issue to be about the misspell bug and open a new design issue for letting (or deciding against) `# fmt: off/on` spanning across unindents.

In the meantime, it appears to happen even if the second comment is missing: [playground](https://black.vercel.app/?version=main&state=_Td6WFoAAATm1rRGAgAhARYAAAB0L-Wj4ACkAFtdAD2IimZxl1N_WlXnON2nzNX9HFvHx6cBGYYzxnKDXUC9bWnmZzMczz8-5oZsWrpdgU6quHPZdEvQmAg39fC5tScCiaDH3kbKBHJ-quOfPTSCcODcQLbiErAffiAAAJEww3dpp7KJAAF3pQEAAAAnngnVscRn-wIAAAAABFla)

```python
class Foo:
    # fmt: off
    1

class Bar:
    # fmt: off
    1
    # fmt: on
```

But not without the class defs.

@felix-hilden 

Thanks!

Now that I think how black might work (I haven't really read the code; but I know it deals with the AST); I can imagine it can be very difficult to support *arbitrary* locations of paired `fmt: off/on`.

The documentation is more or less clear about it:

>  It doesn’t reformat **blocks** that start with `# fmt: off` and end with `# fmt: on`, or lines that ends with `# fmt: skip`. `# fmt: on/off` have to be on the same level of indentation. 

But it can be improved.   Let me first explain how I came up with the first example.  In the actual code from which I derived the first snippet; the first protocol is bigger and has a nice docstring that I want `black` to format.  That's why I started the `# fmt: off` inside the class itself.  The second protocol didn't have a docstring because it's trivial.

I don't think real code would use `fmt: off/on` like this very often; so it might be easier to make the documentation much more explicit about this.   Alternatively, we can fix black to detect missing `fmt: on` when the indentation level is less than the level of the last `fmt: off`.  But I wouldn't know how difficult is to introduce this change in black's parser.

body:
I updated docs in the PR linked above. So some thoughts about this issue:

I think in this situation, assuming we won't change `# fmt: off/on` to allow arbitrary placement, we *should* fail. Currently in the examples presented here, we fail with two different messages: "not equivalent to source" and "cannot parse". We ought to try to catch them and inform the user that `fmt` was used incorrectly. Thoughts?
Agree, this sort of code is incorrect and Black should fail on it, but we should fail gracefully and not with a crash.

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

Black crashes when "fmt: off/on" is used with "with" expression.

**To Reproduce**

For example, take this code:

```python
# file.py
def do_something():
    # fmt: off
    with open('foo') as foo,\
         open('bar') as bar:
        # fmt: on
        raise SomeError()


class SomeError(Exception):
    pass

```

And run it with these arguments:

```sh
black file.py
```

or check in black console online [HERE][ref_console].

The resulting error is:

> error: cannot format black_bug.py: INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced code that is not equivalent to the source.  Please report a bug on https://github.com/psf/black/issues.  This diff might be helpful: ...

**Expected behavior**

Should not crash. I use "fmt: off" and "fmt: on" to prevent moving multiple "with" into one a single line.

**Environment**

```
% black --version
black, 22.6.0 (compiled: yes)
Python (CPython) 3.9.13
```
MacOS

issue.title: Fix a crash when `# fmt: on` is used on a different block level than `# fmt: off`

<!-- Hello! Thanks for submitting a PR. To help make things go a bit more
     smoothly we would appreciate that you go through this template. -->

### Description

<!-- Good things to put here include: reasoning for the change (please link
     any relevant issues!), any noteworthy (or hacky) choices to be aware of,
     or what the problem resolved here looked like ... we won't mind a ranty
     story :) -->

Previously _Black_ produces invalid code because the `# fmt: on` is used on a different block level.

While _Black_ requires `# fmt: off` and `# fmt: on` to be used at the same block level, incorrect usage shouldn't cause crashes.

The formatting behavior this PR introduces is, the code below the initial `# fmt: off` block level will be turned off for formatting, when `# fmt: on` is used on a different level or there is no `# fmt: on`. This also matches the current behavior when `# fmt: off` is used at the top-level without a matching `# fmt: on`, it turns off formatting for everything below `# fmt: off`.

- Fixes #2567
- Fixes #3184
- Fixes #2985
- Fixes #2882
- Fixes #2232
- Fixes #2140
- Fixes #1817
- Fixes #569
